The OS-s-4 vintage block then correctly reports 'VINTAGE: 0 catalog(s) joined (none), 0 table(s)' for SELECT 1, because the table list is DERIVED from the SQL rather than recited. STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN WORKED AROUND: --budget 30 is BELOW comp-heat's own FEDERATED_LIVE_FLOOR_S (200 s), so this criterion can only be satisfied on the REFUSAL path -- which is the correct outcome, because the alternative is raising the budget past 200 s to force a live dispatch, i.e. paying a shared plane to make a criterion look better. THE INVOCATION ALSO MATCHED ITS <expect> BEFORE THIS CELL, inherited from OS-s-1's floor check; the cell's real defect was on the DISPATCH path, where cmd_federated called `run_federated_query(qs)` with neither of the transport's own bounding parameters, giving a fixed 15x40 = 600 s ECS waiter no --budget could shorten. That is fixed and is evidenced under O5-AC2.

Final line: 'OS5-SQL-BOUND BATTERY: 10/10 PASS (denominator 10; 10 child runs, 0 live Trino dispatches -- arm Z is the check, not the claim)'. pytest: '1 passed in 5.04s'. THE ARM THE CRITERION NAMES: '[PASS] G-RED-MUTANT-SQL-RUNS-UNBOUNDED-AND-IS-CAUGHT -- mutant at --budget 250 -> transport received {delay: 15, max_attempts: 40, ceiling_s: 600} (the transport's OWN defaults, a fixed 600 s wait no --budget can shorten) vs production at the SAME budget -> {delay: 5, max_attempts: 45, ceiling_s: 225}'. The mutation restores the literal pre-cell call `run_federated_query(qs)` in a TEMPORARY COPY of comp-heat, and '[PASS] H-MUTATION-ANCHOR-UNIQUE' asserts the anchor occurs exactly once so the mutant cannot silently no-op. THE OTHER EIGHT ARMS: A the order's own invocation refuses and dispatches nothing ('rc=0 | budget: 30 s (flag) | live-banner-absent=True'); B the --sql path at --budget 0.0001 still refuses (row W1-S2's race, re-exercised on the --sql path its original arms did not cover); C the floor is NOMINAL, not elapsed-time -- '--budget 199.9 -> refused (rc=0) ; --budget 200.1 -> dispatched to the STUB (transport received {delay: 5, max_attempts: 35, ceiling_s: 175})', two runs separated by 0.2 s of DECLARED budget and by nothing in wall-clock, so no elapsed-time check could tell them apart; D the ceiling derives from and MOVES with the budget -- 225 s at --budget 250, 375 s at --budget 400, monotone, both under the pre-cell 600 s; E --budget 0 is honoured as UNBOUNDED and the transport receives its OWN defaults with the disclosure line present, so the tool does not invent a ceiling the caller declined; F a waiter timeout is a BUDGET EVENT -- rc=3, 'BUDGET REACHED:', 'ANSWER-STATE: PARTIAL_OR_BLIND', 'results are NOT claimed', 'was NOT cancelled', and no traceback; I --help discloses the bound on --sql; Z the falsifier for this battery's own safety claim -- 'swept 10 captured child-process outputs for the real transport's own dispatch banner ... 0 hit(s)'. REGRESSION: test_os1_budget_battery.py 21/21 PASS, test_os2_path_grain.py 10/10 PASS, test_os4_federated_vintage.py 9/9 PASS, test_comp_heat_battery.py 'Ran 2 tests ... OK', all rc=0.
acceptance.denominator: 10 of 10 arms PASS (printed by the battery itself, its own final line), across 10 child process runs and 0 live Trino dispatches. Stable across 3 direct runs plus one pytest collection.
acceptance.status_reason: The mutant is read at the TRANSPORT rather than in the output: what the caller's budget did or did not reach is a PARAMETER, invisible in any printed line, so a stub that records the kwargs is the only instrument that can see it. Arm D was corrected before this instance was written -- it first hardcoded max_attempts==45 for --budget 250 and FAILED at 44, because the ceiling derives from clock.remaining() at dispatch, already below the nominal budget; the code was right and the expectation was wrong, so the arm now asserts the property (delay 5; ceiling never exceeds what the caller has left; monotone in the budget; under the pre-cell 600 s) and prints the numbers, rather than a constant that would be a brittle red teaching re-tuning instead of reading.

declared_exclusions.item: bounding the REMOTE task's own duration, or cancelling it
declared_exclusions.reason: run_federated_query returns only [{sql, columns, rows}] per query -- the ECS task ARN never crosses that boundary, so there is nothing to pass to ecs:StopTask -- and .tools/_trino_fed.py is not in this order's <paths>. This is limb 3 of NFRA_OUTSET-W1-S2 and it stays ARMED with 2.0.0_SA_COO as disarm owner (row NFRA_OUTSET-W1-S15). The tool now PRINTS the limitation on every dispatch rather than leaving it to the channel.

declared_exclusions.item: a Trino session property such as query_max_execution_time
declared_exclusions.reason: the one mechanism that could bound the REMOTE work rather than the caller's wait; it would mean editing _runtime_script in .tools/_trino_fed.py, which is out of grant. Named because it is the real answer, not because it is unimportant.

declared_exclusions.item: any restriction on the SQL statement itself
declared_exclusions.reason: comp-heat's docstring claims READ-ONLY while --sql passes the statement through unread (row NFRA_OUTSET-W1-S17). Deliberately not built: CLAUDE.md forbids implementing an approval gate on work Andrew did not ask for, and a keyword filter over arbitrary SQL is a FALSE sense of safety -- it reads as enforcement while being trivially evadable, which is worse than a documented gap. The cell asked for a bound on time and cost, and that is what was built.

it stays 0 because OS-s-1's already-drained battery asserts it (arms FEDERATED-DEFAULT-BUDGET-REFUSES-LIVE and FEDERATED-TINY-BUDGET-REFUSES-LIVE). The new non-clean rc 3 is on the NEW dispatch-cut path only, where the caller genuinely has no answer.

declared_exclusions.item: exercising a real dispatched query end to end
declared_exclusions.reason: every arm that needed to be past the 200 s floor used a stub transport instead. A single real dispatch would cost a shared in-VPC Fargate task and 3-4 minutes of a shared Trino coordinator to observe a value the stub reports exactly, and the issuer's own instruction was to prefer arms that prove the bound without dispatching.
